options.option_text: Detest (correct: abhor = regard with disgust and hatred; detest = feel intense dislike for ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. ABHOR = to regard with disgust or hatred; to detest strongly. Synonyms: detest, loathe, despise, abominate. Antonyms: love, cherish, admire, adore. 'She abhors violence in any form.'

options.option_text: Hasten (correct: precipitate (verb) = cause to happen suddenly and quickly; hasten ✓)
Consider (wrong — precipitate implies hasty action, not deliberation)

questions.explanation: B is correct. PRECIPITATE (verb) = to cause something bad to happen suddenly or sooner than expected. Synonyms: hasten, accelerate, trigger, bring about. Note: as adjective 'precipitate' = done very suddenly and without careful consideration.

options.option_text: Confirm (correct: corroborate = confirm or give support to a statement or theory ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. CORROBORATE = to confirm or give support to a statement, theory, or finding. Synonyms: confirm, substantiate, verify, validate, support. 'The witness's testimony corroborated the CCTV footage.'

options.option_text: Revere (correct: venerate = regard with great respect and reverence; revere = feel deep respect or admiration ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. VENERATE = regard with great respect; revere. Often used for holy persons or sacred things. Synonyms: revere, honour, respect, worship, adore. 'Indians venerate the river Ganga.' Antonyms: disrespect, disdain, vilify.

options.option_text: Aggravate (correct: exacerbate = make worse; aggravate = make more serious or severe ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. EXACERBATE = to make something worse or more severe. Synonyms: aggravate, worsen, intensify, inflame, compound. Antonyms: ameliorate, alleviate, mitigate, improve. 'The drought exacerbated the food crisis.'

options.option_text: Affable (correct: amiable = having a pleasant and friendly manner; affable = also pleasant/friendly ✓)
Brusque (antonym — brusque = blunt to the point of rudeness)

questions.explanation: B is correct. AMIABLE = having a friendly and pleasant manner. Synonyms: affable, genial, congenial, personable, charming. Antonyms: hostile, cantankerous, surly, brusque. 'Her amiable nature made her popular at work.'

options.option_text: Reticent (antonym — reticent = not revealing thoughts readily)
Garrulous (correct: loquacious = tending to talk a great deal; garrulous = also excessively talkative ✓)
Laconic (antonym — laconic = using very few words)

questions.explanation: B is correct. LOQUACIOUS = tending to talk a lot; talkative. Synonyms: garrulous, voluble, verbose, chatty, talkative. Antonyms: taciturn, reticent, laconic, reserved.

options.option_text: Disown (correct: repudiate = refuse to accept or be associated with; disown = refuse to acknowledge ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. REPUDIATE = to refuse to accept, deny the truth or validity of, or disown. Synonyms: disown, reject, deny, disclaim, renounce. 'He repudiated the accusations against him.' Antonyms: accept, acknowledge, embrace, support.

options.option_text: First (wrong — penultimate = second to last, not first)
Second to last (correct: penultimate = next to the last in a sequence ✓)
Very important (wrong — a common misconception; penultimate ≠ 'ultimate/most important')

questions.explanation: B is correct. PENULTIMATE = second to last. From Latin: paene (almost) + ultimus (last). 'The penultimate chapter of the book' = the second-to-last chapter. Common mistake: people use 'penultimate' thinking it means 'ultimate' or 'most important' — it means NEXT TO LAST.

B is correct. AMELIORATE = to make something bad better; to improve. Synonyms: improve, better, alleviate, mitigate, rectify. Antonyms: worsen, exacerbate, aggravate, deteriorate. 'The new policy aims to ameliorate poverty in rural areas.'
